text:
Elliot Price: Dropping PR link for structured output page refresh review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/903

Elliot Price: Main open question: do we include a retry strategy in the docs page itself (e.g. validate -> retry w/ “fix JSON” prompt), or keep the page minimal and just link out to canonical examples?

Wei Chen: Skimmed. The new page reads a lot cleaner than the old “JSON mode” one. My concern w/ retry: docs readers will copy/paste and accidentally build an infinite loop / hammer the API.

Henry Cho: +1. We should avoid anything that looks like “just keep retrying until it parses”. But we *do* want to set expectation that schema validation failures can happen and that the right handling is usually a small bounded retry.

Ibrahim Khan: For parity across SDKs we’ve been standardizing on:
- strict schema validation on the client
- max attempts (2–3)
- exponential backoff + jitter
- if still failing: surface error + include raw model text for debugging

I’d prefer docs page has a short callout, and we keep full patterns in redwood-examples + SDK guides.

Sabrina James: Agree. Also the docs page is already doing a lot (introduce schemas, explain how `response_format` works, show a full schema block). If we add a full retry loop, the page becomes “application logic” heavy.

Kira Thompson: From Dedicated/Private side: people running behind proxies/LBs sometimes see partial responses / truncated JSON and will blame structured output. Having *some* mention of “validate, and optionally retry once” helps deflect support, but we should keep it lightweight and point to troubleshooting.

Wei Chen: What about a FAQ entry at bottom:
“Why am I getting schema mismatch / parse errors?” -> “validate, retry up to N, log raw output, and contact support if persistent”

Henry Cho: Works. We should be precise about error naming though. The gateway returns a specific error on schema mismatch now (and some older snippets were doing silent parse + empty object). Docs should say: don’t silently swallow.

Ibrahim Khan: Yup. Also: tool calling + structured output combos can produce “almost JSON” when folks stream and parse too early. The canonical examples explicitly say: only parse after final response event, not per-token.

Elliot Price: On that note, do we want to mention streaming here? Or keep structured outputs page focused and link to streaming page?

Sabrina James: Link only. Otherwise we re-litigate event semantics in every page.

Marcus Lin: Security nit: if we recommend logging raw output, we should say “log with redaction / don’t log secrets”. People will paste customer inputs into logs.

Wei Chen: +1. Maybe: “Capture the raw text in debug logs (redact sensitive inputs)”

Henry Cho: Another nit: please call it “tool calling” everywhere (not “function calling”) per PM alignment.

Elliot Price: Ack, I’ll fix wording pass.

Elliot Price: Proposal for the doc page:
1) Keep main flow minimal.
2) Add a short “Validation + bounded retry” callout box with max attempts + backoff guidance (no full loop code).
3) Add FAQ item: schema mismatch / parse failures.
4) Link to canonical examples repo for full implementations.

Ibrahim Khan: Sounds right. For the callout, suggest language like:
- “Validate the parsed output against your schema.”
- “If validation fails, retry 1–2 times with an instruction to return *only* JSON matching the schema.”
- “Do not retry indefinitely.”

Sabrina James: Also add one line: “If you stream, wait for the final response before parsing.” That’s been a top confusion.

Wei Chen: Works. Keep it as one sentence + link.

Kira Thompson: Can we also add “If you’re behind a proxy that buffers/terminates long-lived connections, see streaming troubleshooting” (link) — but that might be too much for this page.

Elliot Price: I can add that to troubleshooting page instead; keep this page scoped.

Marcus Lin: 👍 on bounded retry guidance. Please avoid recommending “ask the model to fix itself with the same user content” if that content could include secrets. (But that’s probably fine if we keep it generic.)

Henry Cho: Final decision from product side: include a *brief* retry callout + FAQ, but don’t include a full retry code listing on the docs page. Full patterns live in SDK guides + redwood-examples.

Elliot Price: Locked. I’ll update PR 903 accordingly and add links:
- canonical examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (structured outputs)
- troubleshooting page once it lands

Wei Chen: :thumbsup: please tag me on the re-requested review.

Sabrina James: +1 tag me too, I’ll sanity check for copy/paste clarity.

Elliot Price: Will do. Thanks all.
